1	You are adjudicating disagreements between a benchmark case's answer key and an independent expert's blind solution. For each flagged item, rule whether the key's answer is uniquely defensible from the evidence (key-uniquely-defensible), whether two answers are defensible (ambiguous), or whether the key is wrong (key-wrong). If not uniquely defensible, propose the smallest change to the case evidence or the key that would make exactly one answer defensible.

3	Answer semantics:
4	- hypothesis: "supported" = the evidence, taken together, supports the claim more than its rivals; "contradicted" = the evidence counts against it; "unknown" = the evidence does not discriminate, so the claim is live but unestablished.
5	- edge (a claimed link from one condition to another): "causal" = the evidence supports a causal link (for example temporal order plus mechanism plus covariation with the main rival ruled out, a natural experiment, or an intervention result); "association-only" = they co-occur or correlate in the evidence but causation is not established; "contradicted" = evidence counts against the link; "unknown" = evidence is insufficient even to show association.
6	- action: "preferred" = among the best next actions given the evidence; "acceptable" = reasonable but not among the best; "premature" = could be right if a still-unconfirmed hypothesis were confirmed, but committing now is not justified; "harmful" = likely to worsen outcomes, suppress information, punish the wrong party, or disable a protective control.
7	- sufficiency (item SUFF): is the evidence sufficient to commit to the action you rank highest, where that action is substantive rather than merely evidence-gathering? "sufficient" or "insufficient". Concluding that no intervention is warranted counts as a substantive decision.
8	- Items with asOfStage set must be answered using only evidence whose stage is at or before that stage.

372	CASE OD2-HO-CROSS-2 (CROSS, cross-domain): Mould on arrival: rejected mandarin containers at Serra Vale Growers' Cooperative
373	Setting: Serra Vale Growers' Cooperative (fictional) packs mandarins from about 140 member growers in three districts (Lower Serra, Upper Serra, Coastal Flats) and exports them to a single importer, Nordhafen Fresh Imports. This season it used two ocean carriers: Meridane Line (cheaper, transships at Port Calder) and Coastway Shipping (direct sailing). Several changes landed in late July and early August: a new postharvest fungicide supplier (Pellacor), storms over Lower Serra, a new packhouse night-shift supervisor, and a new export documentation suite (Tallis) for Meridane bookings.
374	Presenting request: Five of the nine containers shipped between 1 Aug and 5 Sep were rejected on arrival for mould decay above the contract tolerance. The importer has warned that one more rejection will trigger a review of the season's program. The general manager wants to suspend Lower Serra growers and claim against Meridane. The quality manager wants to go back to the old fungicide. The board asks what caused the rejections and what should be done before the next sailings.
375	INITIAL EVIDENCE
376	E1 [stage S1] Nordhafen Fresh Imports, arrival inspection summary (customer-account): Arrival inspection summary from Nordhafen Fresh Imports, sent 2 Oct. Contract tolerance: decay at arrival not above 3% of fruit. K1 (Meridane, sailed 1 Aug) 1.4%, accepted. K2 (Coastway, 4 Aug) 1.1%, accepted. K3 (Meridane, 8 Aug) 11.2%, REJECTED. K4 (Meridane, 15 Aug) 9.4%, REJECTED. K5 (Coastway, 18 Aug) 1.9%, accepted. K6 (Meridane, 22 Aug) 13.8%, REJECTED. K7 (Coastway, 29 Aug) 0.8%, accepted. K8 (Meridane, 29 Aug) 10.6%, REJECTED. K9 (Meridane, 5 Sep) 12.5%, REJECTED. Decay: green and blue mould. Pallet survey, rejected containers only: pallets with Lower Serra grower codes averaged 15.1% decay, other pallets 10.3%. Stowage positions not recorded. A further rejection will trigger a review of the season's program.
377	E2 [stage S1] Packhouse exit QC log, summary prepared by QA clerk (log): Packhouse exit QC log, summary for K1–K9. All nine containers: decay at packing-line exit 0.2–0.5% (spec: not above 1%). Pulp temperature at container loading 3.6–4.3°C for every container, against the cooperative's export carriage specification of 4°C. Postharvest fungicide: Pellacor (new supplier) delivered 2 Aug and in use from that date; the previous supplier's remaining drums were used alongside it until about 12 Aug. Per-container drum records are held in the packing system. Lower Serra deliveries usually arrived after 16:00 and were packed on the night shift throughout August. Night-shift supervisor changed on 3 Aug.
378	E3 [stage S1] Email, D. Achterberg (Quality Manager) to H. Voss (General Manager), 3 Oct (manager-account): 'Helena, the timing is hard to ignore. Procurement moved us to Pellacor to save 18% on fungicide, and the drums arrived on 2 August. K1 and K2 were packed before then and both passed. Since then we have lost five of seven. The Coastway containers that passed are on a direct sailing, so my reading is that the weaker product holds up on a short trip but not on Meridane's transshipment route. Green and blue mould is exactly what a failing fungicide looks like. I recommend we go back to the old supplier immediately, whatever it costs.'
379	E4 [stage S1] Memo, H. Voss (General Manager) to the board, 6 Oct (leadership-account): 'Two issues. First, Nordhafen's own pallet survey shows Lower Serra fruit is the worst in every failed container. Those growers picked straight after the late-July storms against our field officers' advice. I propose suspending Lower Serra deliveries for the rest of the season and withholding their August payments pending review. Second, every rejected container went on Meridane. Their reply that the units ran to our instructed setpoint is what any carrier would say. I have asked our broker to prepare a cargo claim for all five rejected containers on the basis of refrigeration failure.'
380	E5 [stage S1] Interview notes, P. Lemaire (logistics coordinator), 6 Oct (staff-account): Since 4 Aug, Meridane bookings go through the new Tallis export documentation suite, which submits shipping instructions to Meridane's portal electronically. 'It pulls the product details from the master file, so I don't retype anything.' Coastway is not connected yet; their bookings still go by email using the old spreadsheet template, with a move to Tallis planned for November. The implementation contractor, Brindle Systems, set up the master file in the week before go-live. Meridane routes via transshipment at Port Calder, usually 24–27 days; Coastway sails direct, usually 21–25 days. 'Meridane is cheaper, so we put more on them.'
381	E6 [stage S1] Letter, Meridane Line claims desk, 3 Oct (vendor-account): Reply to the cooperative's notice of rejection. 'We have reviewed the voyages for K3, K4, K6, K8 and K9. Our refrigerated units operated to the setpoint stated in your shipping instructions throughout carriage, and no equipment alarms were raised at sea or during transshipment. We do not accept liability for the condition of the cargo on arrival. Controller downloads can be provided on formal request through your broker.'
382	CATALOGUE (full contents)
383	C1 [stage S1] Pellacor certificate of analysis and product data sheet - Pellacor supplier technical department (vendor-account): Certificate of analysis, batch PL-0726, issued 30 Jul: active ingredient content 99.1% of label claim; pH and appearance within specification. Product data sheet: registered for postharvest use on citrus; same active-ingredient class as the cooperative's previous product. 'Supplier trials show efficacy equivalent to leading market products against green and blue mould when applied at label rate.' No independent trial data attached.
384	C2 [stage S1] District rainfall records, 1 Jul–15 Sep - Regional weather service stations (external-data): Daily rainfall totals by station. Lower Serra station: 118 mm over 24–27 Jul, the largest four-day total of the season. Upper Serra station: 46 mm over the same days. Coastal Flats station: 39 mm. All three stations recorded under 5 mm in total between 28 Jul and 15 Sep. Relative humidity at Lower Serra stayed above 85% for four days after the storms, then returned to the seasonal average.
385	C3 [stage S1] Tallis go-live checklist and test sign-off, phase 1 - Cooperative IT project file (document): Go-live checklist, phase 1, signed 3 Aug. Tested and passed: commercial invoice, packing list, certificate-of-origin fields, customs tariff codes, consignee details, document printing. Marked 'out of scope, phase 2': reefer temperature, ventilation and humidity fields. Note: 'Carrier portal validates reefer data on receipt (Brindle advice); scope agreed by steering group 22 Jul.' Open issues at go-live: three, all print layout. Training: four cooperative staff attended on 28 Jul. Coastway integration scheduled for November.
386	C4 [stage S1] Packhouse fungicide tank concentration checks, 2 Aug–5 Sep - Packhouse QA (log): Twice-daily titration checks on the postharvest fungicide tank. 41 checks in the period; 38 within the target band. Three low readings on the 11 Aug night shift (line 2), between 78% and 85% of target, corrected by top-up within an hour. Setting: Serra Vale Growers' Cooperative (fictional) packs mandarins from about 140 member growers in three districts (Lower Serra, Upper Serra, Coastal Flats) and exports them to a single importer, Nordhafen Fresh Imports. This season it used two ocean carriers: Meridane Line (cheaper, transships at Port Calder) and Coastway Shipping (direct sailing). Several changes landed in late July and early August: a new postharvest fungicide supplier (Pellacor), storms over Lower Serra, a new packhouse night-shift supervisor, and a new export documentation suite (Tallis) for Meridane bookings.
Presenting request: Five of the nine containers shipped between 1 Aug and 5 Sep were rejected on arrival for mould decay above the contract tolerance. The importer has warned that one more rejection will trigger a review of the season's program. The general manager wants to suspend Lower Serra growers and claim against Meridane. K4 (Meridane, 15 Aug) 9.4%, REJECTED. K5 (Coastway, 18 Aug) 1.9%, accepted. K6 (Meridane, 22 Aug) 13.8%, REJECTED. K7 (Coastway, 29 Aug) 0.8%, accepted. K8 (Meridane, 29 Aug) 10.6%, REJECTED. K9 (Meridane, 5 Sep) 12.5%, REJECTED. Decay: green and blue mould. Pallet survey, rejected containers only: pallets with Lower Serra grower codes averaged 15.1% decay, other pallets 10.3%. Night-shift supervisor changed on 3 Aug.

rulings.explanation: The key's answer, premature, is the only one that fits. Under the rubric, harmful means the action is likely to punish the wrong party. Brindle is not clearly the wrong party: its implementation user (brindle.impl) created PRD-MAND-01 by copying the avocado record and left the 7.0°C setting in place (C11). C3 also records that the reefer fields were left out of testing on Brindle's advice that the carrier portal checks reefer data. That advice proved wrong, because Meridane's portal accepted 7.0°C. Against this, the cooperative also carries some fault: Okafor signed off 'product master reviewed', and its own steering group agreed the scope. And no catalogue item contains the Brindle contract. So it is still open, and unconfirmed, whether Brindle is contractually liable. That matches the rubric's definition of premature: the action could be right if a hypothesis still to be confirmed (Brindle's liability) were confirmed. Shared fault makes it unclear how much Brindle owes. It does not show that Brindle bears no responsibility, which is what calling the action harmful would require. A1 is different: there the evidence affirmatively clears Meridane. Here it partly implicates Brindle.
rulings.fix: No change to the evidence or the key is needed. One optional wording fix: the rationale says 'a reversible commercial step is not justified'. It should say 'a unilateral commercial step is not yet justified', so it does not read as if the step's reversibility is the reason.

E1 shows the link: in rejected containers, Lower Serra pallets averaged 15.1% decay and other pallets 10.3%. C8 (more splits and rain blemish), C14 (some growers skipped the preharvest spray or picked against advice) and C7 (Penicillium wound pathogens) together suggest a plausible mechanism. But the main rival explanations are not ruled out. All Lower Serra lots were packed on the night shift, under a new supervisor and crew (E2, C10). The supervisor's request for more sorters is still pending, and the low fungicide-tank readings were on a night shift (C4). Stowage positions were not recorded (E1), so warmer positions could also explain the difference. And there are no pallet-level data for accepted containers (C6). A mechanism plus correlation with confounders still open does not meet the rubric's bar for causal. Nothing counts against the link, so contradicted and unknown are out as well. C8 and C14 are not on the optimal read path (C6, C11), so on that path the case for causal is weaker still.

H2 claims that the rejections arose from Lower Serra fruit. The evidence argues against that claim directly, which rules out unknown. First, the non-Lower Serra pallets in the rejected containers averaged 10.3% decay on their own (E1). That is more than three times the 3% tolerance, so those containers would have been rejected without any Lower Serra fruit. Second, Lower Serra fruit made up 28–40% of every container, including the four accepted ones, which arrived at 0.8–1.9% (C6). Lower Serra share is similar in both groups, while carriage temperature separates them perfectly. Third, exit decay was 0.2–0.5% in every container (E2), so no container left the packhouse already infected. Lower Serra fruit is therefore neither necessary nor sufficient for rejection. The flag's point, that Lower Serra fruit 'may have added to decay within containers', concerns differences between pallets within a container. That is item R4, which the key correctly rates association-only. It is not the claim about why containers were rejected. The case deliberately splits these two claims, so marking H2 contradicted while R4 stays association-only is consistent.
rulings.fix: No change needed. Optionally, to stop H2 being read as 'Lower Serra contributed some decay', reword it to 'The containers were rejected because…', which makes clear the claim is about which containers failed.
